2027-04-22.title: Thursday of the third week after Qyomtho
readings: Surrounded by a cloud of witnesses, looking to Jesus
The widow and the unjust judge: pray always and do not lose heart
2027-04-22.alt: Season of Qyomtho (the Resurrection), the week after the Third Sunday after Qyomtho.
2027-04-22.verse: let us run with perseverance the race that is set before us, looking to Jesus the pioneer and perfecter of our faith
theo: Three and a half weeks after Qyomtho, the joy of Easter has to learn to walk. The first rush of the feast is over; ordinary days have come back, with work, exams, illness and bills. The Letter to the Hebrews speaks to exactly this moment. It has just finished its long roll-call of the faithful of old, Abel and Noah, Abraham and Sarah, Moses and Rahab and the prophets, and now it turns to us: “Therefore, since we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, let us also lay aside every weight and the sin that clings so closely, and let us run with perseverance the race that is set before us.” The picture is a stadium. The runners are on the track, and the stands are full of those who have already finished. St John Chrysostom pictures the saints as spectators who once ran the same course and now cheer us on, so that we may not be ashamed to slacken before such a crowd (Homilies on Hebrews 28, in substance). In the Holy Qurbono our Church names them every time: the Mother of God, the prophets and apostles, the martyrs and confessors, the holy fathers and all the faithful departed. We never run alone.

But the runner does not keep looking at the stands. Hebrews tells us where to fix our eyes: “looking to Jesus the pioneer and perfecter of our faith, who for the sake of the joy that was set before him endured the cross, disregarding its shame, and has taken his seat at the right hand of the throne of God.” Jesus is the pioneer, the one who has already run the whole course, through the Cross and the tomb, and has broken the tape on Easter morning. He is also the perfecter: he will bring our faltering faith to its finish. “Consider him who endured such hostility against himself from sinners, so that you may not grow weary or lose heart.” The Gospel takes up the same danger of losing heart. “Then Jesus told them a parable about their need to pray always and not to lose heart.” A widow, with no money, no husband and no influence, keeps coming to a judge “who neither feared God nor had respect for people,” saying, “Grant me justice against my opponent.” In the end he gives in, only to be rid of her. Then the Lord draws the lesson from the lesser to the greater: if even this judge yields, “will not God grant justice to his chosen ones who cry to him day and night?” God is not the unjust judge; he is the Father. The point of the parable is not that we must wear God down, but that we must not let ourselves be worn down. St Augustine wrote to the widow Proba that to pray always is to keep desire for God alive in the heart without ceasing, and that our set times of prayer rekindle that desire when it cools (Letter 130, in substance).

Our Church gives us a rhythm for this persevering prayer: the seven times of prayer of the Shehimo, from the Evening prayer through the night to the Ninth Hour, so that the whole day is carried to God. Few families can pray all seven, but every family can keep two: the evening prayer together before supper and a short prayer on waking. Jesus ends the parable with a question that is meant for each of us: “And yet, when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on earth?” Faith is found in people who keep running and keep asking. If there is a prayer you stopped making because nothing seemed to happen, a child far from the Church, a marriage under strain, a healing not yet given, take it up again today. Bring it to the Holy Qurbono, where the risen Lord who finished the race gives himself as food for runners who are tired. And remember the cloud of witnesses: ask one saint you love to run beside you this week.
outline: Ask: what prayer have I quietly stopped praying because I lost heart?
Point 1 · A great cloud of witnesses
The stadium full of those who finished the race.
The pioneer who ran through the Cross to the joy beyond it.
Point 3 · Pray always and do not lose heart
The widow who kept coming, and the Father who hears.
“Let us run with perseverance the race that is set before us.”
live: Write down one intention you stopped praying for, and pray for it every evening until Sunday.
Name one habit that slows you down in following Jesus and leave it aside for one week.
2027-04-22.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, pioneer and perfecter of our faith, for the joy set before you you endured the Cross and now you are seated at the right hand of the Father. Keep our eyes fixed on you. Surrounded by the cloud of witnesses, by your holy Mother and all the saints, help us to lay aside every weight and the sin that clings to us, and to run with perseverance. Teach us to pray always and not to lose heart, trusting that the Father hears the cry of his children day and night. When you come, may you find faith in us. You live and reign for ever. Amen.
altar: At the altar the runner who has finished the course feeds those still on the track: in the Holy Qurbono the risen Jesus gives his own Body and Blood as strength for the race.

quick: Hebrews: surrounded by a great cloud of witnesses, we run the race with our eyes fixed on Jesus.
Jesus endured the Cross for the joy set before him; considering him keeps us from losing heart.
The widow kept asking until the judge gave in; how much more will the Father hear his children who cry to him day and night.
2027-04-22.action: Take up again one prayer you had stopped praying, and pray it tonight.
2027-04-22.question: When the Son of Man comes, will he find faith in me?

family.explain: Jesus told a story about a widow who needed help. The judge did not care about anyone, but she kept coming back again and again until he helped her. Jesus says God is much better than that judge: he is our Father and he loves to hear us. So we should keep praying and never give up.
family.intention: We pray for something our family has been asking God for a long time.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing we will keep praying for together every night this week?”

illus: A grandmother in a parish near Pathanamthitta kept a small notebook beside her Shehimo. On one page she had written the names of her six grandchildren, and every evening, after the evening prayer, she read the names aloud. One grandson had stopped going to church when he left for college in Bengaluru, and for eleven years his name stayed on the page. Her daughter once told her it was no use. She said only: the widow did not stop, so I will not stop. In the twelfth year he came home for Easter, sat at the back of the church and stayed for the whole Qurbono. Afterwards he asked her: Ammachi, were you praying for me? She showed him the notebook.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you ran the race before us. Keep our eyes on you and our hearts in prayer. Amen.
share: Since we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses (Hebrews 12:1). Which saint or which person of faith has cheered me on?
Consider him who endured such hostility... so that you may not grow weary (Hebrews 12:3). Where am I growing weary now?
Pray always and not lose heart (Luke 18:1). Which prayer do I need to take up again?
interc: For all who are tired in faith, that they may look again to Jesus and run with perseverance.
For widows and all who have no one to speak for them, that they may find justice.
For judges, lawyers and officials, that they may fear God and respect every person.
For those whose long prayers seem unanswered, that they may not lose heart.
For our parish, that the joy of Qyomtho may become steady, persevering prayer.
pm.close: Father, you never grow tired of hearing your children. Keep us running the race with our eyes on Jesus, keep our prayer alive day and night, and at his coming let him find faith on the earth. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! The Letter to the Hebrews pictures a great stadium. We are on the track, and the stands are full: since we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, let us also lay aside every weight and the sin that clings so closely, and let us run with perseverance the race that is set before us (Hebrews 12:1).

Where do we look while we run? Looking to Jesus the pioneer and perfecter of our faith, who for the sake of the joy that was set before him endured the cross (Hebrews 12:2). He has already finished the course; on Easter morning he broke through the tape of death. Consider him, says Hebrews, so that you may not grow weary or lose heart (Hebrews 12:3).

In the Gospel Jesus tells a parable about our need to pray always and not to lose heart (Luke 18:1). A poor widow keeps coming to a judge who fears neither God nor people, until he gives her justice just to be rid of her. If even he gives in, will not God grant justice to his chosen ones who cry to him day and night? (Luke 18:7). Our God is not that judge. He is our Father.

Jesus ends with a question: when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on earth? (Luke 18:8). Let us answer it with our lives. Take up again the prayer you dropped. Keep the evening prayer at home. Come to the Holy Qurbono for strength, and run with the saints. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Have you ever run in a race at school sports day? When you are tired, the people cheering help you keep going. The Bible says the saints in heaven are like a big crowd cheering for us. And Jesus is at the finish line! Jesus also told a story about a lady who kept asking and asking until she got help. He wants us to keep praying and never give up. What will you keep praying for this week?

intro: Theme: “Let us run with perseverance the race that is set before us, looking to Jesus.”
On Thursday of the third week after Qyomtho: the cloud of witnesses, the eyes fixed on Jesus, and the prayer that does not lose heart.

q: but those who wait for the Lord shall renew their strength, they shall mount up with wings like eagles, they shall run and not be weary, they shall walk and not faint.
Do you not know that in a race the runners all compete, but only one receives the prize? Run in such a way that you may win it.
points.apply: Choose one saint to be your companion this week and ask for his or her prayers each morning.

sub: The pioneer who has run the course.
q: Look to him, and be radiant; so your faces shall never be ashamed.
forgetting what lies behind and straining forward to what lies ahead, I press on toward the goal for the prize of the heavenly call of God in Christ Jesus.
points.apply: Spend five quiet minutes before a crucifix or an icon of the Resurrection and simply look.

points.h: Pray always and do not lose heart
sub: A widow with nothing but persistence.
Not an unjust judge, but a Father.
Will he find faith on earth?
q: Evening and morning and at noon I utter my complaint and moan, and he will hear my voice.
Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all circumstances; for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you.
points.apply: Keep the evening prayer as a family every day until Sunday, and add the one intention you had dropped.

concl: The saints have finished the race and cheer us on; Jesus has run it first and waits at its end.
Persevering prayer is the breath of the runner: the Father never tires of hearing it.
2027-04-22.resolve: Fix your eyes on Jesus, take up again the prayer you dropped, and do not lose heart.
